extracted.intended_audience: taxpayers who receive tips, tax professionals, payroll/reporting entities, and employers
extracted.subtask_description: Final Treasury/IRS regulations implementing section 224 of the Internal Revenue Code defining 'qualified tips', the list of occupations that customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024, and related procedural, reporting, and anti-abuse rules. The document explains statutory criteria, the methodology for compiling the occupations list, applicability dates, limits, and related guidance for taxpayers and reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of qualified tips (section 224(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: "The term 'qualified tips' means cash tips received by an individual in an occupation that customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024, as provided by the Secretary."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory core: qualified tips are cash tips tied to occupations on the Secretary's published list (the List of Occupations that Receive Tips). Only tips received in occupations on that list are eligible for the section 224 deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntariness and payment characteristics requirement (section 224(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified tips must be amounts that "Is paid voluntarily without any consequence in the event of nonpayment, is not the subject of negotiation, and is determined by the payor."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation adopts the statutory three-part payment-characteristic test: (1) voluntary with no consequence if not paid; (2) not negotiated; (3) determined by the payor. Tips failing these characteristics are not 'qualified tips.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified service trade or business exclusion (section 224(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified tips do not include amounts "received in the course of a trade or business that is a specified service trade or business as defined in section 199A(d)(2) of the Code."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For employees, an individual is treated as receiving tips in a specified service trade or business if the employer's trade or business is a specified service trade or business. This exclusion prevents tips connected to SSTBs from qualifying under section 224.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash tips definition includes charged tips and tip-sharing (section 224(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: "The term 'cash tips' includes tips received from customers that are paid in cash or charged and, in the case of an employee, tips received under any tip-sharing arrangement."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charged tips (credit-card/gratuity on a bill) and employee tip-sharing arrangements are treated as cash tips for purposes of the deduction; this supports inclusion of tips even where not physically paid in cash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting/source documentation requirement (section 224(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified tips must be "included on statements furnished to the individual pursuant to section 6041(d)(3), section 6041A(e)(3), section 6050W(f)(2), or section 6051(a)(18) of the Code, or are reported by the taxpayer on Form 4137."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only tips that appear on the enumerated information statements or are reported on Form 4137 qualify for the deduction; the preamble references Notices (e.g., Notice 2025-69) and future form instructions for claiming the deduction and information-reporting transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Security number requirement (section 224(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: "No deduction is allowed under section 224 unless the taxpayer includes on the return of tax for the taxable year such individual's Social Security number (SSN) as defined in section 24(h)(7) of the Code."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxpayers must include the SSN on their return to claim the section 224 deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Married filing jointly requirement (section 224(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the taxpayer is married, "section 224 applies only if the taxpayer and the taxpayer's spouse file a joint return for the taxable year."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Married individuals filing separately are ineligible for the deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dollar limit and modified AGI phaseout (section 224(b)(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The deduction is limited to an amount not to exceed $25,000 in a taxable year and "phases out for taxpayers with modified adjusted gross income over $150,000 ($300,000 for joint filers)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 224(b)(1) sets a hard cap ($25,000). Section 224(b)(2) reduces eligibility for higher-income taxpayers via a phaseout based on modified AGI, which includes certain excluded amounts under sections 911/931/933.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-employed / trade-or-business allocation rule (section 224(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For qualified tips received in the course of a trade or business of an individual (other than as an employee), such qualified tips are taken into account under section 224(a) only to the extent that gross income for the taxpayer from such trade or business (including such qualified tips) exceeds the sum of the deductions allocable to the trade or business for such taxable year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-employed individuals may only take the deduction to the extent the tipped trade's gross income (including tips) exceeds the trade's deductible expenses allocable to that trade; this limits use of the deduction against net losses or fully offset businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and applicability dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 224(h): "No deduction is allowed under section 224 for any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2028." Applicability: "This section applies to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024." Final regs effective June 12, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deduction is temporary (through 2028) and the regulations specify effective and applicability dates. Taxpayers should note the limited window for claiming the deduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement to publish a fixed List of Occupations that Receive Tips (section 70201(h) / 224(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary must publish a list of "occupations that customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024"; only tips received in occupations on that list are qualified tips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute contemplates a single comprehensive list as of the fixed date; the final regulations implement that list. The list is intended to be exhaustive as of the date (though illustrative examples under each TTOC are not exhaustive).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for constructing the List of Occupations that Receive Tips
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treasury and IRS compiled the list based on a review of IRS data (2023 Forms W-2 box 7, Forms 4137, Forms 1040 occupations), legislative history, and survey data; they created a Treasury Tipped Occupation Code (TTOC) mapping to 2018 SOC Codes and used a $100 annual tip reporting threshold and percentages of taxpayers reporting at least $100 in tips within occupations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulators used the best comprehensive data available (tax return data for 2023 and preliminary 2024), supplemented by GITCA program data, the PSID survey, and the House Budget Committee report. They sometimes combined or split SOC codes into TTOCs to better identify tipped occupations and removed non-tipped occupations within SOC groupings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of threshold and 'customarily and regularly' standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treasury/IRS applied a $100 annual threshold (reporting ≥$100 in annual tip income) and relied on dictionary definitions and FLSA guidance (which characterizes 'customarily and regularly' as frequency greater than occasional but potentially less than constant) to determine whether occupations customarily and regularly received tips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explains the choice of $100 annual threshold and contrasts it with the FLSA's $30/month standard; commenters questioned the threshold and requested transparency. The agency defended the data-driven threshold and methodology given statutory differences from the FLSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of occupations with limited customer interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 224(d)(3) and agency approach allow inclusion of occupations that may not have extensive customer interaction (e.g., cooks, dishwashers) because cash tips include tips received under tip-sharing arrangements and the statute does not require customer interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike FLSA guidance that emphasizes customer interaction, section 224's text and the regs permit inclusion of certain back-of-house roles when data indicate customary tip receipt (including via pooling/tip-sharing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustive-as-of-date nature of the occupations list and illustrative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute describes a list as of a specific point in time; the final regulations state that only tips received in occupations on the List of Occupations that Receive Tips are eligible for the deduction and that the List is exhaustive as of that date, while illustrative examples under each TTOC are not exhaustive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is fixed to occupations as of December 31, 2024. Taxpayers may find occupations not listed as illustrative examples but still encompassed by a TTOC. The regs do not contemplate an open-ended evolving list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility and interpretation (transparency and taxpayer responsibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Taxpayers wishing to claim the deduction and entities responsible for information reporting are primarily responsible for ensuring their occupation is on the List of Occupations that Receive Tips; the IRS intends to interpret the occupations in a fair and impartial manner consistent with their commonly understood meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency declined commenter proposals for safe harbors or frequent updates; commenters requested more transparency (e.g., written job descriptions, evidence thresholds), and the agency made some revisions where data supported modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data limitations and treatment of independent contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: The tax-return-based data used consisted primarily of employees (W-2 and Form 4137) and therefore may underrepresent tipped independent contractors because, prior to 2026, information returns for independent contractors did not separately report tips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency supplemented tax return data with survey data and GITCA; it notes information reporting changes effective tax year 2026 that will separately report certain tips for independent contractors and employees, improving future data coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with the FLSA and DOL guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the FLSA uses the phrase 'customarily and regularly' and provides a $30/month tipped threshold and other guidance, the occupations identified under section 224 are independent of FLSA determinations and have no bearing on FLSA status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explains differences in statutory text, purpose, and thresholds between section 224 and the FLSA and clarifies that inclusion on the section 224 list does not alter FLSA classifications or employer tip-credit decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-abuse authority and rules (section 224(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 224(g) instructs the Secretary to prescribe such regulations or other guidance as may be necessary to prevent reclassification of income as qualified tips, including regulations to prevent abuse of the deduction allowed by section 224.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations include anti-abuse rules and other guidance to prevent taxpayers from improperly reclassifying remuneration as qualified tips. The preamble references anti-abuse rules as a substantive component (see table of contents item 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tip-sharing arrangements and related rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations address tip-sharing arrangements (see table of contents item 9) and treat tips received under such arrangements, for employees, as cash tips for purposes of the deduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regs discuss tip pools and tip-sharing; they also noted FLSA requirements about pooling and who may participate, but treat employee tip-sharing receipts as includible in 'cash tips' for section 224 when otherwise qualifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupation classification approach (TTOC and SOC mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treasury Tipped Occupation Code (TTOC) system was created based on the 2018 Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) system; the agency sometimes combined or divided SOC Codes to form user-friendly TTOCs and to remove non-tipped occupations grouped under the same SOC Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occupation names and descriptions in the list are based on the nature of the service provided. The TTOC organizes occupations and provides illustrative examples; the preamble explains that statistics reported in tables are often at the related SOC Code level and may differ from the narrower TTOC.
